summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would set a statutory timetable for increasing Australian overseas aid and establish an independent commissioner to assess how effectively development assistance was used.
Official development assistance would reach 0.5 per cent of Gross National Income by 2015-16 and 0.7 per cent by 2020-21 and subsequent years.
The Minister would report annually to Parliament on aid amounts and shortfalls, while the commissioner would assess relevance, impact, value for money and sustainability.
changes: If aid fell short of the timetable, the Minister would have to explain how future goals would be met.
Commissioner recommendations and the Minister’s responses would be tabled in Parliament.
The Governor-General would appoint the commissioner full time for a term of up to five years.
Money would be appropriated for the commissioner’s appointment and the Act’s functions.
summary.affected: The Foreign Affairs and Trade Minister, the proposed commissioner and developing countries receiving Australian aid are affected.

speeches.speaker: Lee Rhiannon
speeches.brief: The Overseas Aid (Millennium Development Goals) Bill 2013 was introduced to mandate Australia meet United Nations official development assistance targets and establish an Independent Commissioner on Aid Effectiveness.
